title: Primitive Recursiveness of the Aligned Pair Parser
statement: The partial parser on finite Boolean strings that reads aligned two-bit blocks from the left, appending $0$ to the first component for each block $00$ and $1$ for each block $11$, stops at the first block $01$, and returns the accumulated first component together with the untouched remaining suffix is primitive recursive. It is undefined if neither such separator nor a valid preceding sequence of blocks is found.
replaced:
The aligned pair parser is primitive recursive.  This parser reads a Boolean string
in aligned two-bit blocks: the blocks $00$ and $11$ contribute the data bits false
and true, the first aligned block $01$ acts as separator, and any other block (or a
missing separator) is rejected; on success it returns the decoded first component
together with the suffix following the separator.
